review: API34+ endpoint display name matching against bonded Bluetooth devices
decision: No v4 alias change is warranted by Android15 r1: keep getName-based endpoint matching and getName-based uniqueness checks.

scope.search_scope: Official SDK API docs; fixed Telecomm directory metadata; only the three source files listed below. Initial official search queries returned no hits. No fourth source file, master/latest branch, native execution, or device query was used.

sdk_documents.paraphrase: Returns the locally modifiable alias; if no alias, returns the friendly device name; may return null on problems. Apps targeting S or newer require BLUETOOTH_CONNECT.
Returns the cached friendly remote Bluetooth device name, possibly null. Apps targeting S or newer require BLUETOOTH_CONNECT.
Provides an endpoint name; the public API does not promise that all OEM implementations derive it from BluetoothDevice.getName.

findings.result: The Bluetooth branch iterates CallAudioState.getSupportedBluetoothDevices, calls device.getName(), and creates CallEndpoint(deviceName != null ? deviceName : empty-string, TYPE_BLUETOOTH). It does not call getAlias or substitute the generic Bluetooth label here.

A generic Bluetooth resource exists in getEndpointName, but the inspected Bluetooth endpoint-construction branch directly uses getName and does not call that helper. The helper labels other endpoint types.

Telecom retains its private endpoint UUID to Bluetooth address map and can reuse an existing endpoint for the same device address. The app-facing display name does not expose this address map. A reused endpoint may retain the name originally copied during creation.

AudioRoute stores type/address/AudioDeviceInfo. The new route controller packages BluetoothDevice instances into CallAudioState and notifies CallsManager; neither file constructs CallEndpoint or calls getAlias/getName to replace its display name.

v4 captures chosen.getName, checks that it remains unchanged, and compares that same getName string across all bonded devices. Its available endpoint match and endpoint UUID checks align with the selected fixed-tag implementation.

uniqueness_rule.for_reviewed_android15_r1: Compare the selected nonempty getName string with getName of every bonded device, using exact string equality. Also require one matching TYPE_BLUETOOTH endpoint in the currently supplied endpoint list, then retain existing identifier/callback and actual-SCO checks.

examples_are_hypothetical_not_device_obs.implication: Switching the app comparison to getAlias would cause a false endpoint-name mismatch.
Alias uniqueness does not remove duplicate getName endpoint ambiguity; the existing bonded-name rejection should remain.

uniqueness_rule.null_or_blank_name: Remain refused; do not substitute alias or generic label as identity.
uniqueness_rule.oem_alias_endpoint_variant: Not established by this review. Do not add an alias fallback based on an assumed OEM behavior.

next_step: Keep v4 name matching unchanged. This is source compatibility evidence, not new playback progress or actual Pixel/Garmin verification.
